proof_summary: For \(N=201886\cdot3^{39101}-1\), modular computations with the norm-one element \(x=2+\sqrt3\) show \(x^{N+1}=1\) and a gcd condition shows that, modulo every prime divisor \(p\mid N\), \(x^{(N+1)/3^{19545}}\ne1\); hence \(3^{19557}\) divides the order of \(x\). If \(N\) were composite, its least prime divisor would satisfy \(p\le\sqrt N\), while that order is at most the size \(2p\) of the relevant norm-one group, contradicting \(2p<3^{19557}\); thus the exponent \(39101\) yields a prime.
